1#main: Matters practiced on chol haMoed. And it contains 7 seifim. They do not place the bier in the street on chol haMoed lest people become accustomed to eulogy — forbidden to accustom eulogy on chol haMoed; except for honor of Torah scholar; therefore they do not bring deceased to cemetery on chol haMoed until entire grave is prepared and ready.
2#main: They do not tear on chol haMoed except one obligated to tear as stated in siman 340; but one not obligated who wants to tear for honor — forbidden.
3#main: If he heard close tidings on chol haMoed — obligated to tear.
4#main: They do not pass shoulder on chol haMoed and do not give meal of recovery except relatives of deceased; but relatives give meal; and same for Chanukah, Purim, and Rosh Chodesh; when giving meal they give only on upright beds; but on Yom Tov, even second Yom Tov — no tearing, passing shoulder, or meal of recovery; on chol haMoed they give meal for everyone for a sage into the street as they give for relatives — all like his relatives.
5#main: Women on chol haMoed wail — meaning all answer as one; but do not clap hands; on Rosh Chodesh, Chanukah, Purim — wail and clap but do not lament — meaning one speaks and all answer after; for deceased buried — no wailing or clapping; these for ordinary person; but for Torah scholar — on chol haMoed, Rosh Chodesh, Chanukah, Purim — wail and lament as on weekday; these in his presence; not in his absence; and day of tidings even distant is like his presence.
6#main: They say over deceased Tziduk HaDin and Kaddish as usual; and on second Yom Tov; but first Yom Tov since not engaged with deceased — they do not say it: {Rama: Some dispute not saying Tziduk HaDin on chol haMoed (Tur brought authorities); custom in these lands not to say Tziduk HaDin all days tachanun not said (Minhagim); therefore also not when burying after noon erev Shabbat; some say if bury at night do not say Kaddish or Tziduk HaDin (Kol Bo).}
7#main: If relative died before Purim and Purim came — does not interrupt mourning; nevertheless mourning not practiced on fourteenth or fifteenth, only private matters; obligated to send portions; and even though not mourning, they count toward seven like Shabbat.
